set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Public Works Coverage Determination PW 2006-001 (citing PW 2004-016, Rancho Santa Fe Village, Feb 25, 2005) holds that publicly offered conduit multifamily revenue bond financing is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and is not a below-market public loan under 1720(b)(4), because bond proceeds and repayments flow through a private trustee and never enter public coffers (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf). Applies to the bond loan alone; County OC Community Resources loans or other public funds added to the deal can trigger state prevailing wage. The determination addressed publicly offered bonds; confirm treatment if the County privately places the bonds.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false for the bond financing itself per DIR PW 2006-001; Attachment H reopened and is silent on prevailing wage.

reason: DIR coverage determination PW 2006-001 states conduit tax-exempt bond financing is not public funds under Labor Code 1720, so the bond alone does not trigger prevailing wage.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal Davis-Bacon: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (PBV development requirements, labor standards) requires the owner and its contractors to pay Davis-Bacon wages in the case of development involving nine or more contract units, whether or not completed in stages (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153). Applies only to PBVs committed under a development agreement for new construction or rehab; PBVs placed on existing housing with 8 or fewer contract units, or no development activity, do not trigger it. State prevailing wage depends separately on other public funds in the deal under Labor Code 1720.
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage set true per 24 CFR 983.153(c): Davis-Bacon at 9+ PBV contract units in development; existing-housing PBVs are not covered.

reason: 24 CFR 983.153(c) requires Davis-Bacon wages for PBV development involving nine or more contract units.
